newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian money market rate falls to 12 from 14 pct.
newsitem.headline: Croatian money market rate falls to 12 from 14 pct.

text.p: The Croatian average money market rate fell to 12 percent on Monday from 14 percent, thanks to good supply of kuna funds.
Trade totalled 17.8 million kuna and was outstripped by 45 million on offer. Demand stood at 21 million kuna, but was not entirely met as lenders and borrowers failed to agree on terms.

Rates were mostly steady with interbank borrowings ranging from 11 percent call money to 14 percent for one-month funds. Some 9.6 million old loans were rolled over at 11 to 15 percent, depending on length.
The central bank calcualted its kuna midrates for Tuesday weaker at 5.6346 to the dollar and firmer at 3.5583 against the German mark. -- Sandra Kalogjera, Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
